title: Ansel and the Contact
premise: Yara Ravensworth, a financial-crimes investigator who launders the reputations of the powerful, receives a meeting invitation from a handler she buried six months ago. Following it into London's gray market of cutouts and dead drops, she learns her clean-money career was itself a cover: she was groomed as the extraction asset for a defector carrying proof that a summit's host bank moves sanctions money. The defector may be bait to flush out every hidden asset before the summit convenes, and Yara must decide whether to pull him out or let him burn to protect the found family of misfit analysts who are the only people who ever made her feel she belonged. In the end Yara fakes the defector's death, feeds the trap false coordinates, and exposes the bank at the summit—choosing visibility at last, at the cost of the anonymity that kept her safe.
about_author: I. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade tracing money through jurisdictions that officially don't exist. They write thrillers about people whose best work is never supposed to be noticed.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Closing another unattributable case, Yara receives a calendar invite from Marcus Hale—her dead handler—for tomorrow, 9 p.m., a shuttered wine bar in Bermondsey. She verifies his death certificate herself. The beat is cold dread beneath professional calm: someone knows exactly who she used to be.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with a flashback to her recruitment. She walks us through her work scrubbing reputations for clients no one names aloud, establishing her isolation and the small team of analysts—Dev, Priya, old Tomás—who form her accidental family. The invitation gnaws at her. Emotional beat: belonging purchased with complicity.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock, Bermondsey
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The meeting is a dead drop, not a person: Hale's voice on a timed recording reveals Yara was trained years ago as an extraction asset for Operation GLASSHOUSE, and a defector named Anton Vasic holds ledger proof that summit host bank Meridian Capital launders sanctions money. Beat: vertigo—the life she built was someone else's plan.

chapters.title: The Defector's Shadow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Yara tracking Vasic through Vienna's banking district; intercut with an unnamed watcher reporting her movements to a handler called Corvus. Yara finds Vasic paranoid, half-feral, insisting he'll only talk face-to-face with 'the Ravensworth protocol.' Beat: hunter realizing she may be prey.

chapters.title: Family Business
chapters.summary: Yara's POV back in London. Dev notices her encrypted traffic; instead of reporting her, Priya quietly covers for her—and Tomás admits he was Hale's colleague once too. The team becomes co-conspirators. Beat: warmth and terror entwined; found family now shares her risk.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Corvus, Meridian's security chief, reveals the defector is deliberate bait—a lure to expose every dormant asset before the summit. He identifies Yara as the likeliest asset and sets a counter-trap using her team as leverage. Beat: the reader sees the cage closing before Yara does.

chapters.title: The Vienna Extraction
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A tense night extraction of Vasic via freight rail goes wrong when Corvus's team anticipates the route—proof of a leak. Yara realizes only her team knew the plan. Vasic, wounded, tells her the ledger implicates Hale too: he didn't die; he vanished. Beat: betrayal inside trust.

chapters.title: What Hale Left Behind
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Yara deciphers Hale's contingency cache while Tomás confesses he leaked under duress—his granddaughter was taken. Yara chooses forgiveness over exile, cementing the found family. She discovers Hale alive, hiding, willing to testify if Vasic reaches the summit. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Before the Summit
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Forty-eight hours out: the team stages Vasic's death to blind Corvus, plants a false meeting point, and smuggles the real Vasic and Hale toward Geneva. Corvus bites—but partially, keeping a kill team in reserve. Beat: breathless orchestration, love expressed as tradecraft.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Contact
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, Yara's POV. At the summit's edge, Corvus springs the trap; Yara walks into it deliberately, trading her own exposure for broadcast of the ledger. Meridian falls publicly; Corvus is arrested by his own employers' cleanup crew; Hale testifies. Yara, finally visible and named, stands with her team. Beat: identity chosen, not assigned.
